title: credential-orchestra-and-resumable-pullstream-facade-across-py-ts-go
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Customers reported inconsistent reauth behavior and awkward stream resume APIs across SDKs leading to duplicated error-handling in app code. This PR introduces a lightweight cross-language 'credential-orchestra' component plus a resumable pullstream facade implemented in Python, TypeScript, and Go to provide a single mental model for credential fallback, prefetch, and graceful reauth while preserving per-SDK ergonomics. Goals: provide a compact orchestrator API surface that can run in-process or as a thin adapter; expose typed resume tokens for deterministic stream resume; add an adaptive reauth scheduler that prefers fast-path token exchange but falls back to queued refresh; ensure backward compatibility with older token providers via a compatibility shim; bump SDK versions to reflect the ergonomic surface changes. Changes: - Add credential-orchestra core (small state machine): discovery -> prefetch -> attach -> refresh -> fanout; - Implement adaptive-reauth scheduler with tunable backoff and preferred prefetch window; - Introduce resumable PullStream facade in py/ts/go that yields typed events and accepts resume tokens; - Provide compatibility shim for legacy credential providers and an opt-in migration helper for customers; - Add unit and integration tests that exercise cross-language resume semantics and corner cases (expired mid-chunk, refresh race, provider failure); - Update SDK docs and quickstart snippets; - Version bumps: py 2.11.0, ts 1.9.0, go 1.5.3; - Small perf optimization: avoid duplicated KV cache invalidation when orchestration is used; Migration notes: default behavior is backward compatible; to opt into orchestra you set ClientOptions.credentialMode="orchestra". Rolling out: staged feature gate behind env var REDWOOD_ORCHESTRA_ENABLE to allow gradual platform rollout and monitoring.
commits: init: add credential-orchestra state machine and interfaces

feat(ts): pullstream facade + compatibility shim for legacy token providers
feat(go): lightweight orchestrator binding and examples
test: add crosslang resume integration tests
perf: avoid double-kv-cache-invalidation when orchestra attached
chore: bump versions py@2.11.0 ts@1.9.0 go@1.5.3
review_conversation: Arjun: Please add a diagram or state table to explain the orchestra transitions, it's not obvious how prefetch interacts with fanout and backoff. Maya: Added ASCII state table and a short sequence diagram in docs; also added explicit invariants in code comments. Lena: The TS facade types look good but I'm worried about node stream backpressure semantics when resume tokens are replayed; can we run an end-to-end on a real websocket case? Maya: Added integration test that spins up a local WS echo and simulates mid-chunk expiry; test passes in CI. Tom: Request to expose a low-level hook for teams that want manual control of refresh timing for legacy providers. Maya: Added optional PreemptiveRefreshHook to the orchestra interface; it's off by default. Final: approvals from Arjun, Lena, Tom. CI initially had a flaky integration test on macOS runners (timeout); flaky test was rewritten to avoid time-based sleeps and rerun, all checks green.
release_notes: Add credential-orchestra and resumable pullstream facade across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKS. New ergonomic API for deterministic stream resume and adaptive reauthentication. Backward compatible by default; opt-in via ClientOptions.credentialMode="orchestra". Version bumps: py 2.11.0, ts 1.9.0, go 1.5.3.
notes_for_backport: If backporting to release branches, include compatibility shim only; avoid the adaptive scheduler on older runtime images due to different time sources. Bump minor SDK versions and update migration docs.
testing_summary: Unit test coverage added for orchestra state transitions and resume token encoding/decoding. Cross-language integration harness verifies resume behavior across socket disconnects, mid-chunk token expiry, and provider failures. CI matrix: py tox (3.9/3.10), ts jest/node16, go test (1.20). One flaky test on macOS was fixed by removing reliance on wall-clock sleeps. Observability: added span tags for orchestration events for tracing and a dashboard tile to track failed refreshes.
changelist_highlights: SDK ergonomics: unified resume token API, opt-in orchestra, PreemptiveRefreshHook, compatibility shim; infra: added REDWOOD_ORCHESTRA_ENABLE feature gate; docs: migration and quickstart; perf: reduced KV cache invalidations when orchestra attached.
